1.title: Quick Reference Recap and Decision Chooser
1.text: Welcome to Module seventeen: Quick Reference Recap and Decision Chooser. This module covers quick-reference recap and decision chooser. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. A requirement-to-answer chooser for every domain. The names, values and rules that questions use. The distractor patterns and the rule that defeats each.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater Insurance
1.text: Our running case is Tidewater Insurance. Tidewater Insurance. The developer meets the topic of this module. Your job: decide, step by step, which build choice fits.

1.title: Decision Chooser
1.text: Decision Chooser. The figure shows this: The seven decisions that most items test, each with its deciding question.

1.title: D2 Applications and Integration (33.1%)
1.text: D two Applications and Integration (thirty-three point one percent). Waiting user. The best answer is...: Realtime Messages A P I (application programming interface); stream for perceived speed. Module: two, three. Non-urgent bulk work, cost first. The best answer is...: Message Batches A P I (fifty percent off, up to twenty-four h, custom id). Module: three. Same long prefix on every call. The best answer is...: Prompt caching: stable first, volatile last; check usage. Module: three. Hard reasoning versus routine requests. The best answer is...: Effort by task (adaptive thinking); manual budget tokens rejected. Module: three. four hundred twenty-nine. The best answer is...: Back off, retry-after, lower concurrency. Module: three, sixteen. four X X. The best answer is...: Fix the request. Module: three, sixteen. Existing cloud contract and I A M. The best answer is...: Claude through that cloud platform. Module: three.

1.title: D2 Applications and Integration (33.1%), continued
1.text: D two Applications and Integration (thirty-three point one percent), continued. Behavior differs by interface. The best answer is...: The interface adds instructions: recreate them in the A P I request. Module: four. Reproducible behavior. The best answer is...: Pin model I D, version prompts, commit settings. Module: four. Business goal to build target. The best answer is...: Functional, non-functional, infrastructure requirements with measurable criteria. Module: one.

1.title: D1 Agents (14.7%), D5 Models (16.8%)
1.text: D one Agents (fourteen point seven percent), D five Models (sixteen point eight percent). Steps known and must be reliable. The best answer is...: Workflow (chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer). Module: five. Path depends on discoveries. The best answer is...: Agent (tool-use loop). Module: five. Verbose work flooding context. The best answer is...: Subagent (isolated context, summary returns). Module: five, nine. Long-running async, little infrastructure. The best answer is...: Managed Agents. Module: six. Execution must stay in our cloud. The best answer is...: Self-hosted sandbox. Module: six. A rule that must always hold. The best answer is...: Hook or permission rule. Module: six, fourteen. Volume classification. The best answer is...: Haiku-tier model verified by evals. Module: eight. Unsure, balanced. The best answer is...: Start with Sonnet or Opus; step up when evals fail. Module: eight.

1.title: D1 Agents (14.7%), D5 Models (16.8%), continued
1.text: D one Agents (fourteen point seven percent), D five Models (sixteen point eight percent), continued. Reduce cost safely. The best answer is...: Cache, batch, route, lower effort, prune; verify with evals. Module: eight. Output differs run to run. The best answer is...: Sampling is random: constrain with prompts, structure, evals. Module: seven.

1.title: D6, D8, D7, D3, D4
1.text: D six, D eight, D seven, D three, D four. Late-session drift and bloat. The best answer is...: Prune tool output, compact, isolate, fresh session. Module: nine. Vague, inconsistent output. The best answer is...: Specific criteria, format, few-shot examples; iterate with evals. Module: ten. Jason (Java Script Object Notation) fails to parse. The best answer is...: Structured output or strict schema plus defensive parsing. Module: ten. Plausible wrong values. The best answer is...: Validate against the source; shape is not truth. Module: ten. Wrong tool chosen. The best answer is...: Better description and schema first. Module: eleven. Sensitive tool action. The best answer is...: Validation plus approval gate plus idempotency. Module: eleven. Capability shared by many apps. The best answer is...: M C P (Model Context Protocol) server. Module: twelve. Procedure or expertise on demand. The best answer is...: Skill (progressive disclosure). Module: twelve. One app's logic. The best answer is...: Custom tool. Module: twelve.

1.title: D6, D8, D7, D3, D4, continued
1.text: D six, D eight, D seven, D three, D four, continued. stdio M C P server breaks. The best answer is...: Do not write to stdout; log to stderr. Module: twelve. Hidden instructions in content. The best answer is...: Untrusted data: separate, tag, least privilege, screen. Module: thirteen. Never run X. The best answer is...: Pre Tool Use hook or deny rule. Module: fourteen. Key leaked. The best answer is...: Revoke, rotate, remove from history, review usage. Module: fourteen. Team standards in Claude Code. The best answer is...: Committed project Claude dot M D and dot Claude settings.json. Module: four, fifteen. Script or C I run. The best answer is...: claude dash p; stream-json for progress. Module: fifteen. Wrong answers. The best answer is...: Check what the model actually received; replay the request. Module: sixteen. Exam tip: Read the last sentence of the item first, name the binding constraint (latency, cost, security, reliability), then match it to a row of this chooser.

1.title: Names and Values to Know
1.text: Names and Values to Know. Messages A P I. max tokens required; system is separate; stateless; stop reason: end turn, max tokens, stop sequence, tool use, pause turn, refusal. Streaming events. message start, content block start or delta or stop, message delta, message stop, ping, error. Caching. five min or one h; write about one point two five times (five min), read about zero point one times; up to four breakpoints; minimum size; cache read input tokens. Batch. fifty percent off; up to twenty-four h; custom id; no mid-request tool loop. Effort. low, medium, high, xhigh, max; fast mode speed: "fast".

1.title: Names and Values to Know, continued
1.text: Names and Values to Know, continued. Errors. four hundred, four hundred one, four hundred three, four hundred four, four hundred thirteen, four hundred twenty-nine, five hundred, five hundred four, overloaded; S D K (software development kit) retries twice by default. Tools. name, description, input schema; tool use to tool result; is error. M C P. tools, resources, prompts; stdio (stderr logging) and H T T P. Settings. user, shared project (dot Claude settings.json), local, managed. Keys. sk-ant-; shown once; secrets manager; rotate. Exam tip: Exact names matter: max tokens, stop reason, cache control, custom id, input schema, tool result, dot M C P dot Jason, dash p.

1.title: Distractor Patterns
1.text: Distractor Patterns. Parallel realtime calls for a cost problem. Does not lower the per-token price. "Always the largest model" or "always the smallest". Model must meet a measured bar at the lowest cost. Raising temperature or switching to a bigger model for security. Not security controls (and sampling parameters are unsupported on current models). A polite request in the prompt to stop attacks. Not enforceable. Hard-coding shared logic into prompts. Not reusable or maintainable. Trusting confident output. Validate and verify. Rewriting the prompt for an H T T P error. The failure is in the integration layer.

1.title: Distractor Patterns, continued
1.text: Distractor Patterns, continued. Keys in code or the browser. Secrets belong in a secrets manager on the server. Exam tip: A distractor is wrong because it is probabilistic, unenforced, over-engineered, over-privileged or aimed at the wrong layer.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Study order: D two first (thirty-three point one percent), then D five, D one, D six, D eight, D seven, then D three and D four. Core stance: Match A P I to latency, model to task, cache stable prefixes, untrusted content stays data, enforce in code, validate output, locate the failure, keep context lean, reuse through the right mechanism, secrets out of code. Day before: Reread this module and the ten rules in Module zero. In the next module, we continue the course.
